entry.title: Tribute To Disruption: The New Hublot Classic Fusion Tributo Goes Back To The Brand's Origins

media:group.media:title: Tribute To Disruption: The New Hublot Classic Fusion Tributo Goes Back To The Brand's Origins
media:group.media:description:
​@hublot #Hublot #ClassicFusion #MONOCHROMEwatches
It only takes one bold idea to leave a mark. The right concept at the right time, and for the right audience. Back in 1980, Carlo Crocco left such a mark on the watch industry with the concept of Fusion. Daringly combining gold with rubber, a material not associated with luxury at the time, he created MDM Geneve, which later became Hublot.
The singular design of the original MDM morphed into the Classic Fusion and would pave the way for one of the most expressive brands in the industry. And today, Hublot is looking back at its origins with the new Classic Fusion Tributo, a tribute to Mr. Crocco's visionary concept in white or yellow gold. We talk to the creator himself about how the MDM Geneve was born, what it represents to him and, of course, the new Tributo watch.
But that's not all, as we also discover what the Tributo means to Hublot through the eyes of CEO Julien Tornare, and how it possibly hints at the future. This, and more, in the full video! Enjoy!

entry.title: Back in Blue: The Longines Spirit Pilot Autoamtic & Flyback Chronograph

media:group.media:title: Back in Blue: The Longines Spirit Pilot Autoamtic & Flyback Chronograph
media:group.media:description:
​ @longineswatches #Longines #Spirit #MONOCHROMEwatches
What was once black now turns blue with Longines' latest additions to the Spirit Pilot line. Introduced in compact sub-40mm cases last year, the new Spirit Pilot and Spirit Pilot Flyback follow suit in terms of size yet show a bold new look for the dial. Finished in matte blue for both, they give the well-balanced Spirit Pilot series a more contemporary spin.
Split between a Spirit Pilot and a Spirit Pilot Flyback, both watches are identical to last year's editions, apart from the obvious shift in colour. That means we're still dealing with 39mm and 39.5mm steel cases, a very legible dial with luminous elements, and mechanical movements all around. To switch things up, Longines also adds a blue textured rubber strap alongside the well-known steel bracelet. This, and a lot more, in the full video! Enjoy!

entry.title: The Baume & Mercier Clifton Automatic 39 & Perpetual Calendar 40 Ice Blue Editions

media:group.media:title: The Baume & Mercier Clifton Automatic 39 & Perpetual Calendar 40 Ice Blue Editions
media:group.media:description:
​ @baumeetmercier1830 #BaumeetMercier #Clifton #MONOCHROMEwatches
Introduced in 2012, the Clifton collection has quickly become a cornerstone series of watches for Baume et Mercier. Drawing on designs of the 1950s, it was substantially redesigned about a year ago, and now welcomes two very dashing and refreshing limited editions: the Clifton Automatic 39 Ice Blue and Clifton Perpetual Calendar 40 Ice Blue.
Both sharing similar design codes and the Baumatic calibre as a base, the pair is livened up with a light or ice blue dial with a radiant barleycorn guilloché pattern. With dimensions of 39mm across for one, and 40mm across for the other, the pair wears as well as they look. Details such as the elongated indices and Alpha-style hands give it a classy, balanced look overall. This, and more, in the full video! Enjoy!

media:group.media:description:
@PaneraiOfficial #Panerai #MONOCHROMEwatches
Good things will last a lifetime, they say, and the Panerai Luminor is proof of that very statement. Born as a military-issued watch in the mid-20th century, it became commercially available in 1993, quickly becoming a modern-day icon. Panerai now travels back to the roots of the collection, so to speak, with the new Luminor 42 PAM01710, PAM01711 & PAM01714. entry.title: Power, The Saxon Way: The New Lang & Heyne Friedrich III Power Reserve Does Things A Bit Differently

media:group.media:title: Power, The Saxon Way: The New Lang & Heyne Friedrich III Power Reserve Does Things A Bit Differently
media:group.media:description:
​ @langheyne #LangundHeyne #FriedrichIII #MONOCHROMEwatches
As an advocate for high-end, artisanal watchmaking for 25 years already, it's fair to say Lang & Heyne does things a touch differently than others. The brand's unbridled attention to detail, deeply rooted devotion to tradition and an incredibly high level of finishing certainly make the watches stand out. This new Friedrich III Power Reserve is a perfect example of that, and the complication itself makes perfect sense on a manually wound watch.
Where in most watches, the power reserve is directly connected to the barrel with a hand moving up and down as the mainspring winds and unwinds, the team at Lang & Heyne have developed a special differential. It ensures the indication is never under stress, as it's more carried along than wound. The indication itself is akin to those found on historic marine chronometers, with a dotted section that gradually gets smaller the closer it gets to zero.
All this is set in the classically elegant Friedrich III, with signature triple-lug design and a crisp white ceramic dial. At the heart, there's a Grivé-finished section, with red or blue details distinguishing the gold from the platinum edition.
This and more, in the full video! Enjoy!

entry.title: EXCLUSIVE: The NEW Rolex Perpetual Padellone, With Annual Calendar & Dynapulse Escapement!

media:group.media:title: EXCLUSIVE: The NEW Rolex Perpetual Padellone, With Annual Calendar & Dynapulse Escapement!
media:group.media:description:
​@ROLEX #Rolex #Padellone #MONOCHROMEwatches
Rolex brings back an iconic watch from the late 1940s with the introduction of the new Perpetual Padellone. It brings together a classic annual calendar display and the revolutionary Dynapulse escapement, as first seen in the Land Dweller. The name is derived from the 1949 Ref. 8171 Triple Calendar, affectionately nicknamed "Padellone" by Italian collectors.
The Perpetual Padellone introduces the new Calibre 7190 and puts it in the Perpetual 1908 case. Available in rose gold or platinum, it comes with a white or ice blue dial depending on the material. As a first, we now also see the beautifully elegant Settimo bracelet in Everose gold. This, and more on Rolex' latest, and perhaps most elegant and complex watch yet, in the full video! Enjoy!

entry.title: The Otsuka Lotec Watches Everyone Is Looking For! A rare chance to see four side by side!

media:group.media:title: The Otsuka Lotec Watches Everyone Is Looking For! A rare chance to see four side by side!
media:group.media:description:
Industrial Time, Reimagined in Japan
Otsuka Lotec has developed a very coherent approach based in industrial design and unconventional time displays, and the No.5 KAI, No.6, No.7.5 and No.8 show how far that idea can be taken.
The No.6 looks like a compact instrument, with retrograde hours and minutes arranged across arched scales.
The No.7.5 takes its cues from vintage cameras, using three lens-like openings for jumping hours, minutes and seconds.
The No.5 KAI features three rotating hour satellites travelling across an arched minute track. The No.8 tells time with a jumping-hour disc with a retrograde minutes display in a rectangular, control-panel-like case.
All four share Katayama’s raw, straight-grained finishing and an emphasis on mechanical behaviour. All are powered by Miyota automatic movements with proprietary modules to create the unusual indications. All are Japan-only and difficult to obtain.

entry.title: The NEW Maurice Lacroix Aikon-IC Frozen Carbon Series Is All Kinds Of Cool.

media:group.media:title: The NEW Maurice Lacroix Aikon-IC Frozen Carbon Series Is All Kinds Of Cool.
media:group.media:description:
A decade ago this year, Maurice Lacroix launched the quartz-powered Aikon collection, with mechanical versions following in 2018. Based on the design cues from the 1990s, it proved a smash hit. After a wide range of colours, materials and complications, the collection welcomed the next chapter last year, with the introduction of the Aikon-IC. Now, a year on, the Aikon-IC range expands with the Frozen Carbon series!
Blending the edgy design codes with a mix of materials, the collection of six is split between three limited editions and three standard versions. All feature a carbon dial with bronze or titanium powder, or coloured resin inclusions baked into it, resulting in a pretty striking look. Add to that ceramic bezels, integrated quick-change straps, a solid automatic movement, and the Aikon-IC certainly makes a statement! This, and more, in the full video! Enjoy!

entry.title: Back For Good: The NEW Louis Vuitton Tambour Spin Time Collection, Now Permanently Available

media:group.media:title: Back For Good: The NEW Louis Vuitton Tambour Spin Time Collection, Now Permanently Available
media:group.media:description:
​ @louisvuitton #LouisVuitton #MONOCHROMEwatches
First released in 2009 as part of the emblematic Tambour collection, the Spin Time is, without a doubt, one of the most recognisable creations of Louis Vuitton horlogerie. The idea, a dynamic display using 12 rotating cubes as a modern interpretation of the classic jumping hour complication, was inspired by the overhead flap panels that show timetables in airports, another reference to travel.
Following the return and revamp of the concept with the Taiko limited editions of 2025, the Louis Vuitton Tambour Spin Time now makes a return as a permanent collection, with 5 different references. We talk to Michel Navas, master watchmaker and co-founder La Fabrique du Temps Louis Vuitton, and Matthieu Hegi, Artistic Director for La Fabrique du Temps Louis Vuitton, about the history and evolution of the Spin Time concept, as well as the new collection.
This, and more, in the full video! Enjoy!

entry.title: The NEW TAG Heuer Carrera Chronograph Sport Collection Is Firing on All Cylinders

media:group.media:title: The NEW TAG Heuer Carrera Chronograph Sport Collection Is Firing on All Cylinders
media:group.media:description:
@tagheuer #TAGHeuer #Carrera #MONOCHROMEwatches
Born in the heart of racing, the TAG Heuer Carrera remains one of the most enduring sports-chronographs. It followed in the footsteps of a many stopwatches and chronograph watches before it, and introduced in 1963, the Carrera would become one of the most iconic watches in TAG Heuer's portfolio for a very simple reason: the clean dial, sharp case profile and intuitive layout of the subdials.
On the occasion of the 2026 Formula 1 TAG Heuer Gran Premio de España in Madrid, the brand ushers in the next chapter for the sportiest take on the Carrera legacy. The new Carrera Chronograph Sport series has a redesigned case, refreshed dials and a familair movement, but of course retains all the Carrera hallmarks. This, and more, in the full video! Enjoy!
